fields.description: Position in the conversation, 1-based. Also the cursor the frontend polls with.
fields.label: Seq

fields.description: Set while an assistant message is still being written, token by token, by a streaming turn. The row exists so a poll can watch its `text` grow; its `blocks` are empty until the stream ends, which is why runner._history skips a message with no blocks. Always 0 by the time a turn finishes — including a failed one, which runner.run_turn clears on its way out.
fields.label: Is Partial

fields.description: Set on a user message sent as a `/skill`: the OS Agent Registry skill_slug that was invoked. `runner.run_turn` reads it to decide whether the turn opens with an agent dispatch.
fields.label: Skill Used

fields.description: The arguments the skill was run with, as sent. Validated against the pack's Input Schema before the run.
fields.label: Skill Arguments (JSON)

fields.description: Which screen the user was on when they sent this, as the client reported it (e.g. `orders`, `item/ABC-1`). Recorded for context and analytics; nothing dispatches on it.
fields.label: Screen

fields.description: Concatenated text blocks, denormalised for display. Empty for a tool-only message.
fields.label: Text

fields.description: The Anthropic content-block list verbatim. This is the source of truth replayed to the model; `text` is derived from it.
fields.label: Blocks (JSON)

fields.description: Display meta per file on this message, as JSON. Two kinds, told apart by `kind`. An upload (kind absent or "upload") is positional: the first len(attachments) blocks ARE its attachment blocks, which is how runner._elide_old_attachments finds them. A generated file (kind "artifact") is not positional — it rides on an assistant message whose blocks are prose and tool_use, and is a download chip rather than context.
fields.label: Attachments (JSON)

fields.description: Records the user named with `@`: [{kind, value, label, hint, …}]. Denormalised for display, like `attachments` — the model reads them from a block ahead of the question, not from here. Written by `chat/mentions.resolve`, so every value was re-checked against its source at send time; the client's own labels and dates are never stored.
fields.label: Mentions (JSON)

fields.description: Follow-up questions offered under this reply, as a JSON array of strings. Written by `chat/suggest.attach` once the turn's answer has settled, on an assistant message only. Display-only and advisory: nothing reads it back into the model's context, and an absent or malformed value simply means no chips.
fields.label: Suggestions (JSON)
